extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, agents, examiners, and legal practitioners operating in British colonial jurisdictions (late 19th-century patent practice)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and standards governing the application, examination, amendment, enforcement, and revocation of patents in various British colonies (e.g., Victoria, Tasmania, Trinidad, Western Australia), including procedural requirements, grounds for opposition/revocation, and remedies for infringement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent term length
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents are always granted for fourteen years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patents cover the entire colony for fourteen years subject to maintenance payments (e.g., payments before expiration of the third and seventh years). In some colonies prolongations/extensions may be obtained for inventions of merit (terms not exceeding fourteen years; other jurisdictions allow further terms up to seven years or, exceptionally, fourteen).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of earlier foreign patents on colonial patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents expire with the determination of any earlier foreign patent for the same invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In some colonies (e.g., Tasmania) patents granted locally will not prevent use in foreign ships in colony waters and will expire if an earlier foreign patent for same invention is determined. There are also provisions allowing local patents to be obtained within specified time after foreign patent with priority dating to the foreign application (e.g., within seven months of UK application in Tasmania; within one year in Victoria for foreign inventions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional protection between application and sealing
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisional protection is granted for the period between the date of application and the date of sealing the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisional protection may only be granted on very full provisional specifications in some colonies. No legal proceedings for infringement can be taken until the patent has been granted, but inventions are protected from consequences of use and publication between application and sealing. Publication of complete specification before sealing means no proceedings for infringements committed before publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may apply for a patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person, whether a British subject or not, may apply for a patent; the applicant may be the actual inventor, his assigns, the inventor jointly with assigns of part interest, legal representatives of a deceased inventor, or (where inventor not resident) any person to whom the invention has been communicated by the inventor or his assigns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special residency or procedural requirements may apply (e.g., some foreign applications require the applicant to be resident in the United Kingdom). Joint applications and corporate bodies are permitted; infants and women and executors may apply/obtain patents subject to rules described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and accompaniment of application
rubrics_metrics.description: The application must be made in the prescribed form and must be accompanied by either a provisional or complete specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications to be left at or sent by post to the Patent Office in the prescribed form; applications are referred to an examiner together with the specification; forms and office rules govern procedure (forms indexed in manual).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner duties and report criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner must ascertain and report whether the nature of the invention is fairly described, whether the application, specification, and drawings are prepared in the prescribed manner, whether the title sufficiently indicates the subject-matter, and whether, to the best of the examiner's knowledge, the invention is not novel or already in the possession of the public (with consent of inventor).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners report on these matters and other queries the Commissioner may require; the examiner's report may lead to refusal or a requirement to amend; examiner's reports are not published or open to public inspection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner/Comptroller discretion on acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: On the report of the examiner the Commissioner (or Comptroller) may refuse the application or require its amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The applicant may appeal from any adverse decision to the Law Officer, who must hear the applicant and the Commissioner and decide whether to accept the application; the Comptroller/Commissioner has powers to require amendments of documents and to dispense with evidence; decisions to be notified to parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits for filing complete specification
rubrics_metrics.description: If a complete specification is not left with the application, it may be left any time within nine months from the application; if not, the application is deemed to have been abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commissioner has power to extend the time for leaving the complete specification for one month; failure to file timely will render application abandoned and specification not to be published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance advertisement and opposition window
rubrics_metrics.description: When the complete specification is accepted the Commissioner must advertise the acceptance and the application is then open to public inspection; any person may give notice of opposition within two months from the date of the advertisement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opposition grounds are limited to specified matters (fraudulent acquisition, communication issues for non-resident inventors, prior patent, want of novelty or prior publication/use, or that the complete spec describes a different invention than the provisional). Opposition heard and determined by Commissioner with appeal to Law Officer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for opposition to grant
rubrics_metrics.description: Opposition may be on grounds that applicant fraudulently or without authority obtained the invention, that the invention has not been communicated to the applicant by the actual inventor (if non-resident), that the invention has been patented in the colony on an earlier application, that the invention lacks novelty or has been published or publicly used, or that the complete specification describes an invention other than the provisional specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opposition is limited to these grounds and must be filed within statutory period; opponents must have interest; proceedings similar to England; appeal to Law Officer possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sealing date effect and provisional limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent is sealed as of the day of application, but no legal proceedings can be taken in respect of any infringement committed before the publication of the complete specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although sealing relates back to date of application, enforcement rights (suits for infringement) are conditioned on publication/sealing per local rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification amendment powers and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: A patentee or applicant is empowered to amend the specification by disclaimer, correction, or explanation; amendments must not substantially enlarge or alter the invention claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments may be opposed; where litigation for infringement or revocation is pending, leave of the Court is required to apply for amendment and must generally be by disclaimer; the Court's discretion is absolute; amendments allowed by Comptroller or Law Officer may be questioned in court; amendments ought to be allowed at patentee's peril when doubtful; clerical corrections may be allowed; amendments when made must be advertised; conditions (e.g., restriction on recovery of damages for pre-amendment use) may apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for amendment under section 18
rubrics_metrics.description: When an amendment is made under the statute (section 18), a written request for leave must be made, the amendment must be advertised, and any person may give notice of opposition within one month; the Comptroller will notify opposition to the applicant and hear and decide, subject to appeal to the Law Officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no opposition appears, the Comptroller may decide whether and on what conditions to allow the amendment; the Law Officer may also hear appeals; form and rules for application for amendment are prescribed (forms referenced).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on amendment by disclaimer
rubrics_metrics.description: A disclaimer may reject claim to parts where both combination and subordinate parts are claimed, but may not strike out a whole claim and insert a claim to a subordinate part; disclaimers should leave sufficient matter to support the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclaimer practice: may cut down claims (e.g., limit methods to particular described methods); disclaimers must be applied carefully; historical case law guides the permissible scope of disclaimers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment opposition requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Opponents to an amendment must have an interest; grounds of opposition are specified; the Comptroller may impose conditions on granting leave but cannot award costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opposition to amendments follows particular time limits and procedural steps; costs rules vary and may be governed by the Law Officer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Register of Patents contents
rubrics_metrics.description: A Register of Patents is to be kept containing chronologically all patents granted, with names and addresses of grantees, notifications of assignments and licences, memoranda of deposit and filing of specifications and disclaimers, amendments of patents and specifications, and of expiry, revocation, or other determination of patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assignments and licences should be registered; certified office copies of documents are receivable in evidence; registry rules and forms apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prolongations/extensions of patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Prolongations may be obtained of patents for inventions of merit which have not been remunerative, for a term not exceeding fourteen years (some jurisdictions allow further specified extensions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures and requirements for extension (including petitions, accounts, and possible hearings) are provided; some colonies provide for Board/Commissioner review and require showing of merit and lack of remuneration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confirmation of invalid patents in special cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Confirmation of invalid patents may be obtained where a court has found that a portion of the invention was old at the date of the application but other parts were new.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are statutory procedures for confirmation under limited circumstances; parties may petition for confirmation subject to evidence and court findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for revocation of patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceedings for revocation may be taken on grounds similar to those in the British Patents Act (e.g., want of novelty, lack of invention, non-patentable subject-matter), with additional colonial grounds such as the invention not having been communicated by the actual inventor or his assignee in communications patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revocation proceedings may be brought in Supreme Court; remedies and procedural aspects (issues, evidence, appeals) follow patterns similar to British law; scire facias procedures may be abolished in some colonies and replaced by alternative proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patents and Crown use
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent rights are good against the Crown, but the Crown may use the invention for public service on terms agreed upon or, failing agreement, on terms settled by arbitration or by the Court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Crown officers may use inventions under statutory provisions (e.g., for war purposes or public service); the Crown does not guarantee patent validity; misuse or misrepresentation to Crown may render patent void.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies for infringement and procedural prerequisites
rubrics_metrics.description: Actions for infringement may be brought in designated courts (e.g., Supreme Court or divisions of High Court), but cannot be brought before the patent has been granted nor for infringements committed before publication of the complete specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Available remedies include damages, account of profits, injunctions, delivery up or destruction of infringing articles; plaintiffs cannot have both damages and account of profits in the same action; plaintiffs may lose damages for infringements committed while renewal fees unpaid; particular procedural requirements include delivery of particulars of breaches, discovery, interrogatories, inspection of documents, production of models, and trial without jury unless otherwise ordered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may sue for infringement
rubrics_metrics.description: Registered proprietors and certain assignees may bring actions; unregistered assignees generally cannot; exclusive licensees cannot sue without joining the patentee; assignees of parts may bring separate actions, subject to registration and notice rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical recommendation: purchasers/assignees should register assignments and perform searches prior to purchase; legal nuances govern suits by trustees, survivors of joint assignees, and unregistered owners under particular factual circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Particulars, discovery, and pre-trial procedure in infringement actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Particulars of breaches must be delivered; discovery and interrogatories are used; inspection of documents may be ordered; production of models before trial is generally refused; trials are ordinarily without jury unless otherwise ordered; factual issues may be referred to a referee whose report is equivalent to a jury finding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessor may be called; scientific witnesses, functions of judge and jury, and admissibility of patentee's evidence on meaning of specification are governed by case law described in the manual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actions to restrain threats (groundless threats remedies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Remedies are provided to any person aggrieved by groundless threats of legal proceedings (action to restrain threats), including injunctions and damages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such actions may be brought under statutory sections; plaintiff in a threats action must show due diligence in commencing and prosecuting an action for infringement; interpretation of 'due diligence' and kinds of threats (letters by solicitor, notices to users, private letters to customers) are discussed; interlocutory injunctions in threat actions must not be moved ex parte and may be refused where defendant undertakes to bring an infringement action with due diligence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of documents by Comptroller/Commissioner
rubrics_metrics.description: The Comptroller/Commissioner has powers to correct clerical errors and to authorise amendment of specifications and documents; discretion should not be exercised adversely to applicants without giving opportunity to be heard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General powers of amendment, ability to dispense with evidence, correction of clerical errors, and requirement to notify parties of decisions are laid out; certificates under comptroller's hand are prima-facie evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication rules for specifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifications are not published unless the applications are accepted; the acceptance of a complete specification is to be advertised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an application is abandoned or void then the specification is not to be published; publication in a colony within priority period will not necessarily invalidate a patent where priority claims are timely (e.g.,Tasmania rule on publication within seven months).

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority claims from United Kingdom or foreign filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants who have applied for protection for an invention in the United Kingdom may be entitled to a patent in the colony with the same date as the UK protection provided the colonial application is made within specified priority periods (e.g., seven months in Tasmania; one year for foreign inventions in Victoria).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication in the colony within the priority period shall not invalidate the patent; forms for communication from abroad and priority procedures are prescribed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability of chemical processes and products
rubrics_metrics.description: Chemical processes and products may be patentable; cases as to patentability and infringement of patents for chemical processes and products are reviewed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manual references authorities and case law on when chemical processes/products are patentable and on infringement principles specific to chemistry (see cited case ranges).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims and construction of specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete specifications must contain claims; specifications and claims are to be construed according to ordinary meaning and with reference to the state of knowledge when prepared; benevolent construction applied, with words and drawings considered together; prior specifications may show anticipation; technical terms may be explained by evidence but patentee's own evidence as to meaning is inadmissible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims construction must consider whole context; when two meanings possible, rules for construction apply; claims may be appendant; case law cited for guidance (sections on interpretation and construction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patents for foreign inventions and registration
rubrics_metrics.description: No person can receive a patent for an invention previously patented in Great Britain or any other country, but the Governor may grant letters of registration to the holder or assignee of any such patent upon payment, and such letters shall be deemed letters patent and have the same force.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some colonies provide route to register foreign patents locally by payment (e.g., 15L mentioned) and such registrations are treated as local patents under the Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Death of inventor and applications by representatives
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent may be obtained by the legal representatives of a deceased inventor if the application is made within specified time after death (e.g., within twelve months in Victoria; other mentions of six months for representative applications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural forms and timing for applications by executors/representatives are prescribed; patent may be sealed within twelve months after death in some cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibitions not prejudicing patent rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Exhibition of inventions at industrial or international exhibitions will not prejudice patent rights if the exhibitor gives the required notice of intention and applies for protection within the statutory period (e.g., twelve months from opening of exhibition).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory notice and subsequent application within time safeguard rights; specific procedural steps required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalties for false marking and imitation of patentee's marks
rubrics_metrics.description: Penalties are imposed on persons marking goods with the name of a patentee without written leave, or marking goods 'Patent' with intent to imitate a patentee's stamps or marks, or selling articles as patented in the colony when not, for the purpose of deceiving the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criminal or statutory penalties described; enforcement and remedies may apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compulsory licences power and grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: The Governor in Council (and in some contexts the Board of Trade) may grant compulsory licences where satisfied that by the patentee's default the patent is not being worked in the colony, the reasonable requirements of the public are not supplied, or where any person is prevented from working or using to the best advantage an invention of which he is possessed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No appeal from some compulsory licence orders (Board of Trade), and the power to impose and the procedures/rules (including making rules) are described; terms, remuneration, and registration of licences are regulated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees, stamps, and payments
rubrics_metrics.description: Government fees and stamp duties are payable on applications, patents, and for maintenance (examples: stamp on a petition 50 dollars in one colony; fees about 11/10s on application; fees of 2L/10s before expiration of 3rd and 7th years; other specified sums for extensions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to pay prescribed payments may cause patent to cease; forms and schedules prescribe exact fees; fees vary by colony and by action (application, advertisement, maintenance, extension).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on recovery of damages after amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments may carry a restriction on the recovery of damages for use of the invention before the amendment (i.e., recovery may be limited).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts/Comptroller may impose conditions on amendments including limits on retrospective damages; historical cases and statutory sections (e.g., under old and new law) provide guidance on how damages are affected by late amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition to amendments time limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person may give notice of opposition to an amendment within one month after its advertisement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comptroller to notify opposition to applicant, hear and decide the case subject to appeal to Law Officer; if no opposition appears the Comptroller may decide unopposed applications and impose conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: No publication of examiner's reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners' reports are not to be published or open to public inspection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports remain internal to the Patent Office; applicants may receive decisions and required amendments but not full reports for public perusal.
